items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: So I got his number and I called Rozelle, and he accepted.

ctx.x: Yeah, Hobart Banks. So I went and called Kansas City, called the union, and wanted to know if there was anybody they could recommend, you know, a piano player, and you know I always dwelled on

that reading, and they said yes, there's one young man, if he's interested, Rozelle Claxton, he'll play anything you want and he's a nice arranger. So I got his number and I called Rozelle, and he accepted. He said you're going to New York? I said yeah, and he said what are you paying? I said Rozelle, we don't work for anything less than scale around here, but I don't know what it's going to be there, I don't know what kind of gigs they're going to put me on, but you ask anybody about my reputation and you'll get…

So then I said I will wait and see when exactly we're going to leave and I'll let my man work on, because he's been very fair with me--Hobart--I said when I get some idea of when we would leave, I'll get you in time, a couple of weeks before we're going.
